entries.notes: Martin-approved Q2 delta (2026-07-21 sweep). Publish already ran {{query}} via render_query with publish_page_allowed filtering; BEGIN_QUERY containers were inert source. Fail-before (worker-run, Sol/high): 2 publish_begin_query tests fail pre-fix. Full publish suite 34 pass + whole tine-core 514 pass (manager-run).

The release workflow now enforces the same symbol-table gate on the canonical APK. Android 9 device confirmation remains desirable but is no longer the only protection against recurrence.

entries.title: Explicit sparse-v2 app activation drains legacy authority, routes whole-root watcher input through one actor, and refuses unproven clean shutdown
entries.notes: The app persists stable caller-owned activation identities only after every tracked legacy Graph lease drains, while graph refresh and migration share the same transition lock, then publishes exactly one sparse actor or a visible retryable/blocked binding. The recursive root watcher closes its installation interval with one full reconciliation, keeps nested and case-variant Markdown/Org events incremental, and ignores explicit unmanaged file events. The journey activates a pre-populated nested Unicode graph without rewriting its bytes, reopens its authenticated aggregate bootstrap baseline, authors and queries through the exact adjacent-tagged actor wire, imports an external edit through the watcher queue, reaches Safe shutdown, exposes stopped runtime as retryable, reopens authenticated LocalActive state, and proves legacy routes remain refused. entries.title: Managed-storage activation retains one authenticated bootstrap baseline and does not publish one durable projection receipt per existing page
entries.notes: The accepted bootstrap already publishes byte-identical per-path projection evidence in one immutable shadow manifest, but the current activation prototype replays the ordinary durable projection protocol once per page before opening reconciliation. The replacement must durably bind and freshly reopen that exact publication, build one bounded manifest locator pass, use an ordinary authenticated receipt when one exists and otherwise use the exact bootstrap entry only at its bound page/path/frontier, and keep untouched Markdown byte-exact. Activation creates zero ordinary bootstrap receipts; a later real projection or accepted import creates the ordinary receipt that supersedes the immutable fallback across restart. Corrupt, duplicate, missing, stale, or cross-workspace/endpoint/archive/graph evidence fails closed without live Markdown or SQLite authority fallback. Structural counters and the release scale receipt enforce constant durable activation commits, one aggregate scan, and bounded point reads independent of graph size.

entries.title: Managed-storage activation and post-activation actor commands stay off the async command thread while preserving exact graph authority

Two nested Unicode synthetic scales retain ordinary references, properties, and tasks; instrumentation records source files, bytes, blocks, and per-phase elapsed time and rejects plainly superlinear shared construction.

entries.title: A cold graph is joinable only from one complete canonical supported shared descriptor with no ambiguous v2 residue

entries.title: Two sparse-v2 devices explicitly share one descriptor-bound lineage and converge bounded filesystem-provider delivery without authorizing partial or conflicting evidence
entries.notes: Covers commit-last prepare-share and crash-resume from SharePrepared, incremental clean join beyond 4,096 provider entries and 8 MiB, both SharedActive roles across restart, reopening more than 64 settled manifests without historical replay, crash-resumable dependency-closed publication including unsafe local-manifest repair after private pending-marker creation failure, independent poll-mode provider delivery, coalesced incomplete-manifest rechecks after adversely reordered exact object delivery, nested nonstandard Unicode Markdown/Org paths, reordered and duplicate delivery, partial bootstrap and split-genesis refusal, dirty unique local-tail refusal, partition/rejoin, receiver-local projection, superseded-frontier rollback refusal, and convergence. A canonical generated Syncthing or Dropbox conflict copy is removed only after exact path, canonical-content, byte-equality, and no-follow retirement proof; differing, absent-target, malformed, or ambiguous evidence remains byte-exact and visibly blocks without graph writes. Continuously unstable full-scan epochs retain their fence and yield to retry backoff after one retry rebase. Tauri exposes bounded explicit prepare/join actions only inside the experimental sparse-v2 Settings flow, keeps provider polling separate from graph-wide reconciliation, and replaces stopped handles with retryable reopen slots after a transient post-transition reopen failure.

entries.title: Provider staging siblings and vanished callbacks cannot wedge later inbound work or Safe shutdown
entries.notes: Exact safety/interoperability contract: only direct-child Syncthing staging siblings with the documented Unix/macOS .syncthing.<payload>.tmp or Windows ~syncthing~<payload>.tmp shape are non-authoritative in both full scans and exact callbacks; invented Dropbox sibling names and malformed canonical names remain visible and fail-closed. Authenticated restart/full reconciliation also pages the complete accepted sequence: every ordinary accepted batch must retain an exact local manifest, exact provider manifest, or digest-bound recovery mirror before Safe, including non-tip A in A→B→C. Recoverable local authority is republished idempotently; deleting canonical provider, recovery link/blob, and local manifest refuses reopen/Safe until local recovery evidence returns, after which the bounded audit repairs provider authority.

entries.title: Accepted-history audits retain exact progress across transient provider failures
entries.notes: A bounded accepted-sequence audit owns an exact retry cursor until it validates the current acceptance root. One-shot provider-read and repair-publication failures at accepted non-tip A in A→B→C fail closed as RecoveryBlocked, remain visible as provider work, and resume in the same live actor. The cursor advances only after the current entry is validated or durably repaired; recovered ticks restore canonical manifest plus digest-bound recovery evidence and reach Idle/Safe without a restart, full provider scan, or manifest/object directory enumeration.

entries.title: Joining cannot irreversibly block on a provider manifest that is only temporarily absent
entries.notes: Exact data-safety contract: Blocked shared.dirty-unique-tail requires a private durable local-authorship receipt written only after LocalMutation acceptance. The canonical receipt digest binds batch/manifest fingerprint, accepted event and prior/post frontier, workspace, lineage, device, endpoint, graph resource, authoring session, and promoted LocalActive runtime. Stable provider absence is never provenance: provider-staged/foreign archive evidence and missing, corrupt, or tampered receipts remain retryable LocalActive state without enrollment mutation across same-process retry and restart. A genuinely locally authored independent tail retains its receipt across restart and still enters terminal Blocked without changing graph bytes.

entries.title: One enrollment operation owns incremental join state while ordinary actor work interleaves
entries.notes: Deterministic barriers pause a multi-turn join after it releases ordinary operation ownership. A conflicting descriptor and prepare_shared both reach the dedicated enrollment mutex and remain serialized until the owning join completes; the exact two-pass traversal proves the conflicting call cannot clear and restart PendingSharedJoin. A status request still acquires ordinary operation ownership and completes during the between-turn pause without changing the join outcome.

entries.title: Large shared-enrollment cuts retain constant state and perform only linear streaming checks
entries.notes: The deterministic join fixture retains more than 4,096 valid immutable provider objects and 8 MiB. Instrumentation requires exactly two complete provider-entry passes, one provider-cut comparison, one constant-size recovery-summary comparison, zero history-proportional entries retained by PendingSharedJoin, at most one recovery relation accumulation per streamed provider entry, and at most one exact recovery-link membership read per streamed local entry. Provider and local cuts use domain-separated cryptographic count/XOR summaries with filesystem-unique path and manifest set semantics; public operation authority is released between incremental cursor turns.

entries.title: Reverse-delivered provider histories use dependency-indexed readiness work while retaining every blocked batch
entries.notes: The fail-before/pass-after stress receipt used a 96-batch linear history delivered newest-first: the indexed scheduler converged with exactly 96 manifest registrations while the prior pending-deque scan performed 9,216 readiness inspections. The always-on 24-batch regression preserves the same quadratic discriminator without adding a four-minute suite cost. A focused index neighbor covers multiple parents, an already-active synthetic base head, duplicate registration, unrelated acceptance, exact edge work, and deterministic sibling wake order. Existing shared-provider journeys continue to cover duplicate exact delivery, incomplete manifests becoming complete, restart reconstruction, publication repair, status visibility, and Safe-shutdown refusal while inbound evidence remains blocked.

entries.title: Routine provider work stays bounded to exact ingress instead of re-auditing lifetime archive history
entries.notes: At d691664e each provider-work turn reopened ObjectStore and validate_namespace enumerated objects plus batches, then fully decoded and canonically validated every lifetime object and manifest. The fail-before regression could not satisfy the retained-counter bound. The pass-after fixture runs nine bounded provider turns over a twelve-batch historical archive: the old path models exactly 18 whole-namespace enumerations and at least 539,199 historical bytes, while the retained Arc path adds zero enumerations and charges 17 manifest inspections, 68 object inspections, and 92,524 bytes to exact ingress/admission in the final recorded release-mode run. Exact byte totals are fixture-derived rather than hard-coded because runtime identities may vary; the test enforces the invariant ratios and successful projection. Authenticated activation/restart keeps the complete ObjectStore namespace validation.

entries.title: SharedActive startup discovers immutable device frontiers without replaying settled provider history
entries.notes: A genuine Safe reopen over more than 64 settled manifests enumerates one device head, authenticates only the exact manifests selected by that bounded head payload, and reads zero provider objects or broad historical manifest paths. Unseen device tips walk exact immutable manifests and digest-addressed objects through the dependency index; empty prototype namespaces fall back once and migrate automatically. Complete namespace repair withholds every head and Safe until bounded recovery-mirror backfill plus canonical manifest/object closure repair settle, while retiring each exact manifest-bound crash-ordering intent after that batch's durable repair. The permanent regression uses an isolated test-only head-scan cap of 8 over 12 accepted historical batches and a mirror-before-canonical crash cut; the production cap remains 4,096. Crash cuts before head publication and before old-head retirement, unsafe reopen, duplicate/reordered device heads, generated conflict copies, malformed evidence, and deleted own heads remain bounded and cannot let Safe outrun durable discovery publication. Superseded-head retirement also converges when provider deletion wins before the first local remove, and a later redelivery is retired through the ordinary journal path, including after completed-retirement provider evidence disappears.

entries.title: Recovery-covered provider heads preserve missing canonical ancestor availability for stale peers
entries.notes: Every ordinary manifest publication durably writes an exact batch link and immutable digest-addressed recovery copy before canonical manifest visibility. Recovery authority is bound to the exact accepted-frontier acceptance sequence and state digest: each newly accepted local or provider batch invalidates the prior authority and enters a bounded exact mirror queue, while uncovered legacy state uses bounded cursor backfill. Only a durable current-root covered head can initialize authority on reopen, and no covered head or Safe can outrun mirror, canonical manifest, required object, or dependency-closure repair. Normal intact reopen authenticates only bounded head-selected tips and reads no recovery copies or historical namespace. Permanent same-document regressions cover a missing middle canonical ancestor and the stronger reordered case where a previously covered receiver accepts canonical/object bytes without the mirror, authors a child, crashes, and cannot publish a covered child head or reach Safe before local mirror backfill. After restart and queue settlement, deleting only the middle canonical still lets a stale third peer reconstruct and converge from duplicate/reordered child, head, link, and blob delivery without either author returning. Crash cuts before recovery and after recovery but before canonical, generated conflicts, corruption, and deletion of both exact copies block visibly.

entries.title: Provider-visible immutable publication intents recover a complete manifest stranded before its covering frontier head
entries.notes: The permanent crash cut publishes immutable objects, canonical descriptor-bound intents, and matching manifests, then stops before a covering frontier head or watcher callback. A normal-startup receiver with an older valid head uses an isolated cap of 4 to discover 6 foreign intents across explicit cursor-preserving chunks. The regression proves the first boundary is neither EOF nor Safe and cannot publish a head, every intent and batch converges without a broad manifest/object scan, and only an actual EOF plus a covering receiver head permits complete foreign-intent retirement and genuine Safe. A two-device deletion-replication regression additionally proves that when a peer retires the author's intent first, the author's later covered retirement settles without a local journal record, accepts a subsequent peer page, and reaches Safe instead of starving inbound work. Missing or mismatched manifests and uncovered intents remain retryable, and the production per-chunk cap remains 4,096.

entries.title: Clean shutdown cannot publish an own head ahead of paused imprecise frontier discovery
entries.notes: A deterministic post-publication crash cut pauses an imprecise head cursor after descriptor discovery, installs a previously unseen foreign recovery-covered head and its complete batch, then recovers a concurrent local publication before requesting shutdown. The durable own head at the cut must already cover both local and foreign tips and current manifest recovery; descriptor/head/intent discovery remains bounded and does not enter manifest/object full-scan history. After the cut, own intent retirement settles and genuine Safe remains bounded. The provider-head oracle rejects tips without current manifest recovery coverage.

entries.title: Incomplete foreign delivery neither strands local publication nor gets outrun after its objects arrive
entries.notes: Realistic two-device helpers deliver manifests independently from immutable objects. The complete-delivery control converges and reaches Safe. In the frontier-decoupling attack arm, one device retains the foreign manifest as visible inbound work while publishing four unrelated local pages: every accepted local frontier gets a durable recovery-covered device head and its covered publication intent retires instead of accumulating. Safe remains refused while foreign objects are absent; restart restores the pending manifest, and late exact object delivery converges it. A second deterministic arm gives foreign and local no-op batches the identical content-addressed object set. The foreign manifest is staged first without that object; local admission then writes the shared object without a provider callback. A post-head crash cut proves the foreign batch is admitted and recovery-covered before the own head becomes durable. At exact base 6ae78827, the first arm failed with no advanced own head and intent counts [1, 2, 3, 4]; against the rejected frontier-decoupling patch before the arrival fix, the second arm failed because the own head omitted the now-Ready foreign batch.

entries.title: Two offline authors union concurrent frontier heads without either branch returning through the other endpoint first

Provider dependency registration and blocked rechecks use authenticated accepted-frontier containment, including manifest-less synthetic and transitive accepted ancestors; page-specific projection authority preserves the exact stale-write fence across unrelated concurrent catalog heads.

The neighboring unrelated-frontier external-delete regression remains covered so the correction does not weaken intentional delete authority.

entries.title: Config filename-policy changes cannot rename an exactly owned oplog page or journal on a later external edit

A real old-path to new-path move still adopts the destination decode, and explicit Tine rename remains the graph-wide RenamePagesAndRewriteReferrers operation.

entries.title: A deterministic projection refusal terminalizes its durable work so restart can drain following pages

entries.title: Case-only page renames retire the old portable-path owner before acquiring the new spelling

Scheduler coverage requires the old Absent work before the new Present work for both casing directions and neighboring Unicode portable aliases; platform-gated integration coverage exercises the native case-insensitive filesystem when available.

entries.notes: Fail-before: the minimized Markdown `- a\n\n` unit and projection regressions failed because the final block raw retained newline trivia also owned by SerializeOpts, producing SpanInstrumentationMismatch; the independent verifier then proved the first correction still rebound blank lines and a promoted collapsed heading by depth-first ordinal after insert/delete/reorder. Accepted Markdown and Org formatting, including final and inter-block blank lines, CRLF, no final newline, preambles, importer-promoted collapsed headings, literal fences/source blocks/logbooks, and multiple blocks, now remains document-owned formatting. Edited projections carry only receipt-proved locator-to-BlockId ownership into the singular guarded serializer; sparse ID-less blocks without such proof are locally canonicalized, and a collapsed heading remains unbulleted only for the same sole semantic root. Nested insert/delete/reorder, same-count reorder, ID-less and ID-bearing neighbors, changed content without reorder, collapsed-root insertion/reorder, guarded serialization, and reparsed semantic equivalence are covered.

entries.notes: Fail-before: the independent verifier used a fixture whose logical name, kind, and path already agreed and changed only round-tripping CRLF/blank-line formatting. Reconciliation produced zero semantic operations, then OperationTransaction's correct non-empty invariant converted that no-op into UnsafeInput. The no-op now has a separate sealed formatting material lane: it publishes endpoint-local intent/base/completion authority, replaces the bounded completed-path baseline only after authenticating the prior receipt and unchanged semantic frontier, and never publishes an operation batch. Crash after intent is recovered after a full Graph/receipt/archive-engine/SQLite/tail restart; exact bytes survive, and a subsequent real semantic edit renders from the adopted formatting baseline.

entries.title: Editor title changes remain one atomic logical rename across Graph, oplog, SQLite, projection, and restart
entries.notes: Fail-before: a public editor save changed Markdown title:: from Editor Title Before to Editor Title After while preserving the blocks. Graph::open observed the new title immediately, but authoritative oplog replay, SQLite, and the restarted editor retained Editor Title Before. Editor saves now use the canonical external-document parser and the identity decision shared with import, preserve a title-only edit's physical path, and atomically compose logical rename, parser-derived kind, final content, collision checks, referrer rewrites, and every affected page. Shared semantic scenarios cover Markdown and Org title add/change/removal, existing and new Page/Journal transitions, nested and nonstandard paths, policy changes, no-op reimport, and two restarts.

entries.notes: Fail-before at bc08c72e: two honest offline replicas renamed one PageId to NFC and NFD spellings sharing one canonical key. After full provider union and restart, each retained its local exact title and provider recovery never completed. One whole authored exact-name event must win by causal order, then stable (BatchCausalDot, BatchId) order for concurrency, without normalizing the winning UTF-8. Fixed-provenance reversed delivery also swaps explicit-title and filename-fallback authorship to prove both presence/removal winner directions.

entries.title: Provider-delivered nested pages converge even when receiver parent directories do not yet exist
entries.notes: Fail-before: an honest offline device created notes/provider-created/deep/physical-source.md and published it through ordinary external-file admission. After complete provider delivery, receiver crash/restart, and duplicate redelivery, a receiver lacking only provider-created/deep remained permanently blocked with authenticated expected-path authority missing and never projected the page. Pre-creating only that parent chain made the exact scenario converge. Projection input capture now reports a stably missing ancestor as semantic absence while ordinary files, symlinks/reparse points, special entries, permission failures, and traversal races remain errors. Present publication reaches the retained-capability recursive writer; a retry resumes after a synced partial chain, while a proven nested tombstone completes without creating parents. The original duplicate-delivery/restart scenario now drains provider work and produces parser-visible receiver bytes.

entries.title: Windows projection and SQLite lease safety use stable public held-handle filesystem APIs
entries.notes: Fail-before: hosted Windows run 30507282266 at exact candidate 7792d3062936e28c2da2089693fd9f644e43305e failed to compile because projection_file_link_count used unstable std::os::windows::fs::MetadataExt::number_of_links and entry_file_identity resolved file_attributes on cap_std metadata to a private implementation method. Projection link count now comes from GetFileInformationByHandle on the already-held file handle, and capability metadata attributes use explicit public cap_fs_ext::OsMetadataExt dispatch. Existing no-follow opens, pre-open and held-handle reparse checks, single-link refusal, identity validation, and error classification remain unchanged.

entries.title: Managed storage reopens promptly after an unclean shutdown even when its reconstructible resume accelerator is unavailable
entries.notes: Fail-before on 92edd261 against the permitted 1,045-file anonymized graph copy: ordinary pending-save crash takeover adopted its resume point in about 0.2 seconds, while forced accelerator unavailability replayed five bootstrap parts in 30.9 seconds locally (the user observed about 58 seconds on slower hardware), emitted about 338 MiB of filesystem output for a 1.3 MiB graph, and failed the 10-second gate. Fixed on fe5dfb7f by reconstructing the immutable bootstrap once in the existing detached authoring engine, migrating that authenticated candidate into the resume path, and replaying only post-bootstrap history in the enrolled engine. The exact fail-before fixture then reopened in 2.36 seconds, adopted bootstrap generation 5, replayed zero bootstrap generations through enrolled recovery, and preserved the original accelerator-refusal reason.
